info.title: Aventy
info.description: Aventy public API v1. Authenticate every request with an API token created in Settings → API tokens, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens carry scopes (orders:read, orders:write, products:read, products:write, geo:read, webhooks:manage); requests missing the required scope get a 403. Errors always use the envelope `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Monetary amounts are numbers in Algerian dinars (DA). Lists use cursor pagination. AI assistants can also connect over MCP at `/mcp` (OAuth 2.1, store-bound, two-phase writes) — see `/llms.txt` for the primer.

200.description: Acknowledge: a malformed envelope will not become valid on retry.

get.description:
Each type keeps `slug` and `name`, and adds `kind` (`home` or
`stopdesk`), `storefront_orderable` and `order_delivery_type` — the
`delivery_type` value to send to POST /orders to order this type, or
null when the type cannot be ordered through the API. `meta.free_shipping`
is true when the calling linked site offers delivery (SAT-SITES-1: set
per site, false for every other key).

**Required scope:** `geo:read|storefront:geo.read`
get.summary: List the delivery types available for this store

get.description:
`price_home` / `price_express` / `price_stopdesk` are the grid rates,
unchanged. Added: `free_shipping`, `types[]` (each type's rate and the
`amount` the customer pays — 0 when the calling site offers delivery), and, when
`stopdesk_id` names one of the store's pickup offices in that wilaya,
`stopdesk` with that office's own price and amount. An unknown office, or
one of another wilaya, is a 422.

**Required scope:** `geo:read|storefront:geo.read`
get.summary: Delivery fees towards a wilaya (home, express and stopdesk prices)

200.description:
ZIMOU-DEFAULT-CARRIER-1 — no grid and no usable carrier: refused
by name, without any carrier call. Same success envelope and
`data` shape as a priced answer (prices null), so a storefront
reading `data.price_*` keeps working, plus a stable machine
code. It used to be a 500: DeliveryManager built a Yalidine
client on empty credentials and the carrier's 400 escaped.

get.description:
`id` is the office's carrier id — stable across the weekly resync, and the
value to send as `stopdesk_id` to POST /orders. `commune_id` is the
platform's commune (null when the referential has no match), `price` the
amount the customer pays for this office (0 when the calling site offers
delivery, null when no rate is stored).

`name` is the carrier's own name and may repeat across a whole wilaya
(Zimou Express): `partner_name` — the company operating the counter, null
when the carrier publishes none — and `address` are what tells offices
apart. Sorted by commune, then price, then partner.

**Required scope:** `geo:read|storefront:geo.read`
get.summary:
Pickup offices of a wilaya for this store, from the stored list only —
never a live carrier call: a wilaya without an office answers an empty
list

post.description:
Receives status-update webhooks from Yalidine, Economiqua or Zimou Express.
The {token} is the store's webhook_token — no other authentication needed.

Which dialect a body is read in comes from the STORE the token resolves
to, never from sniffing the payload: `delivery_provider` is the one fact
we hold that the caller cannot influence.

Zimou Express (see {@see self::handleZimouEvent()}):

    { "event": "package.status.changed",
      "package": { "tracking_code": "ZIM-…", "order_id": "…",
                   "status": "LIVRÉ", "status_id": 8,
                   "reason": null, "reason_id": null } }

Yalidine family — two payload shapes are accepted:

  Nested + batched (observed contract):
    { "type": "parcel_status_updated",
      "events": [ { "event_id": "...", "occurred_at": "...",
                    "data": { "tracking": "...", "status": "...", "reason": null } } ] }

  Flat (what this endpoint accepted before):
    { "tracking": "YLD-XXXX", "status": "Livré", ... }

An EMPTY raw body is the carrier's URL-validation ping, not a malformed
webhook.

get.description:
Two jobs, both strictly read-only:

 1. CRC challenge. Yalidine validates a webhook URL by calling it with
    `?subscribe=1&crc_token=<50 chars>` and demands the raw token back as
    the entire body. Anything else — JSON, quotes, a trailing newline —
    reads as "n'a pas répondu avec la bonne valeur du crc_token".
    `subscribe` is answered when present but never required.
 2. Liveness probe, so a carrier checking the URL does not read a 405 as
    a broken endpoint.

The {token} is never resolved and never used beyond a 6-char log prefix:
the response is byte-identical whether the token exists or not, so this
is no oracle for enumerating tokens. A real merchant token has already
leaked to facebookexternalhit through a webhook URL pasted into a
messaging app; echoing a caller-supplied value mutates nothing, but
nothing that mutates may ever be added here.

get.summary: List the communes of a wilaya

post.description:
Called by the Apps Script installed on the user's Google Sheet.
Payload: { spreadsheet_id, rows: [...], from_row }
Signature: HMAC-SHA256 in X-GSheets-Signature header.

Gating + signature are checked synchronously (security first); the import
itself is queued so a large pushed batch never times out the webhook.

Shopify sends the HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256.
We verify it against the store's shopify_webhook_secret.
Only processes "orders/create" topic.

SHOPIFY-WEBHOOK-ID-1: every notification leaves one `[webhook.shopify]`
trace line (store, topic, webhook id, content type, HTTP status, order
created). A signed orders/create whose body names no order — not JSON,
or JSON without `id` — is refused with a 400 instead of crashing into a
500: Shopify then exhausts its retries and drops the useless
subscription. Never the body in a log line, only its size.

message.const: Unreadable notification: the body names no Shopify order.

post.description:
WooCommerce sends the HMAC-SHA256 in X-WC-Webhook-Signature.
Topic is in X-WC-Webhook-Topic (e.g. "order.created").

200.description:
Acknowledge to LF anyway so it doesn't retry on a non-retriable error.
The failure is captured in the events log.

get.description:
`from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive) are calendar days in the
store's timezone (Africa/Algiers): an order created at 23:30 UTC on
30/09 is a 01/10 order. Timestamps in the response stay in UTC (…Z).

**Required scope:** `orders:read`
get.summary:
List orders (cursor-paginated). Filters: source, status, from, to,
search (order number, customer name or phone)

post.summary:
Create an order from a direct payload (items inline, geo by id or
name). Idempotent on external_id: replaying the same (source,
external_id) returns the existing order with a 200 instead of a 201.
Also supports the Idempotency-Key header (exact response replay, 24h)

post.description:
Body (multipart/form-data):
  - file            : required, CSV or XLSX file (max 5 MB)
  - error_strategy  : optional — "continue" (default) | "stop"
  - duplicate_strategy : optional — "skip" (default) | "accept"

**Required scope:** `orders:write`

patch.description:
`commune_id` must be an existing commune of the order's wilaya — the
`wilaya_id` sent in the same call, or else the one the order already
has. Otherwise the call fails with 422 and `commune_id` names the reason.

Changing `wilaya_id` without sending `commune_id` keeps the current
commune only if it belongs to the new wilaya; otherwise the commune is
cleared and the order comes back with `needs_review: true` (200, never
a refusal).

**Required scope:** `orders:write`
patch.summary:
Update customer/delivery details. Only pending or confirmed orders can
change; anything further in the pipeline is a 409

message.example: Only pending or confirmed orders can be updated.

patch.description:
SF-UNRESOLVED: moving an order INTO the confirmed funnel (`confirmed`,
`shipped`, `delivered`, `returned`) requires every cart line to name an
article of the catalog. An order still holding an unidentified line
answers 422 with code `incomplete_cart` and the references at fault;
`pending` and `cancelled` are unaffected.

**Required scope:** `orders:write`

get.description:
`view=storefront` (SF-PRODUCTS) swaps the merchant payload for the
shop-window one, defaults the listing to active products, and turns the
response into a cacheable resource (ETag + Cache-Control) so a satellite
polling every 5 minutes mostly gets 304s.

**Required scope:** `products:read|storefront:products.read`

partner_name.description:
The company actually operating the pickup point, verbatim:
the carrier's own label for a third party, never normalised.
Present on 778/778 offices of the reference account across 9
companies, so the merchant knows whose door to send the
customer to. Empty string → null, so the UI omits the line
rather than rendering a blank badge.

commune_id.description:
The CARRIER's commune numbering, as everywhere else in
store_delivery_centers (YAL-STOPDESK-2). The local commune is
resolved from the name by StopdeskCommuneResolver.

price_known.description:
CART-RAWTEXT-1: false when the imported line carried no price —
unit_price and subtotal then read 0 as a placeholder, not a price.

stopdesk_name.description: SAT-PILOT-1 — the office's name as it was when the order was placed.

stopdesk_partner_name.description: SAT-RELAIS-1 — what tells the office apart: its operating company and address, frozen too.

fulfillment_source.description:
ZE-WH-AUTOSHIP-1 (T6) — `local` | `zimou_warehouse` | `mixed`.
Posé ici plutôt que dans chaque consommateur : cette ressource
sert l'API v1 ET les outils MCP, donc un seul point à tenir.

imported_from.description:
CARRIER-IMPORT-1 (T1) — `zimou` | `yalidine` | null, au même
endroit et pour la même raison : un consommateur d'API ou un
outil MCP qui additionne des commandes doit pouvoir écarter
celles qui ne sont pas nées ici, sans avoir à le déduire de
`source`. `imported_at` accompagne la valeur parce que
`created_at` porte, lui, la date du COLIS chez le transporteur.

price.description: NULL = inherits the parent product price

stock.description:
Variant aggregate (VARIANTS-2/C); may be negative while the
merchant still owes a ventilation covered by the product's
non-ventilé stock.

customer_name.description:
A lead often holds nothing but a phone number — the customer
stopped before the name field. OrderIntakeService already falls
back to the phone number for the display name.

shipping_fee_to_confirm.description:
SAT-PILOT-1 — the storefront had no fee grid to show the customer
("fees confirmed by phone"): the order is taken, priced by the
platform and flagged for the agent. Never a reason to invent an
amount on either side.

shown_shipping_fee.description:
SAT-SITES-1 (2d, decision 8) — on an abandoned cart captured by a
linked site's key: the delivery fee the site SHOWED the customer
(whole DA) and the delivery type it belonged to. Optional, stored
on the cart as sent, compared at conversion; never billed.

abandoned_external_id.description:
The `external_id` of the abandoned cart this order comes from,
carried by the REAL order: the platform then marks that lead
recovered, links the two and drops it from the callback list.
Satellites prefix lead ids ("ABN-…") so a lead and the order the
same visitor later places never collide on the idempotence key —
which is also why matching on an identical external_id would
never fire, and why this field is the link. SF-ABANDONED (D5).

source.description:
How the storefront satellite tags what it posts: `storefront`
files a real order, `storefront_abandoned` files an abandoned
cart — a callback lead with relaxed fields, inert in every flow
(see /llms-full.txt). Omitting it files the order under `api`.
The whitelist is closed on purpose: a free-form source would let
a caller impersonate a sales channel, and dodge the blacklist net
the OrderObserver hangs on storefront traffic. SF-SPLIT-1,
widened by exactly one value in SF-ABANDONED.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
